Lig]]. The club was founded in 1954 by [[middle-class]] merchants and artisans in response to their perceived alienation within the city's then most popular club, [[Adana Demirspor]], who were supported by workers, financed by landowners, and governed by [[Turkish State Railways|TCDD]] staff. The two clubs first played against each other in 1956, with the match becoming known as the [[Adana football derby|Adana derby]]. Both clubs have fiercely competed for citywide support and domination since then, and each club's fans believe their club to be the true representation of the city of Adana. In addition, Adanaspor's home ground, [[Adana Stadium]], is shared with their archrivals, which intesifies their matches even further.[http://www.tff.org/Default.aspx?pageID=395&kulupId=3603 5 OCAK – ADANA DEMİRSPOR] tff.org {{in lang|tr}}, accessed 4 June 2010 Adanaspor's jersey colors, orange and white, symbolize oranges and cotton, the main harvests of the city.[https://www.altinsehiradana.com/Makale/adana-derbisinin-tarihi-2/965/] Altınşehir Adana, accessed 23 January 2020 Adanaspor were one of the most successful clubs of the Turkish Football League in the 1970s and early 1980s. ''Toros Kaplanları'' ([[Taurus Mountains|Taurus]] Tigers) were the Runners-up for the [[1980–81 1.Lig|1980-81 season]], having participated at the [[Süper Lig|top division]] for a total of 22 years. The club also competed in the [[UEFA Cup]] for three years.[http://adanaspor.com.tr/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=44&Itemid=31 Tarihçe] adanaspor.com.tr {{in lang|tr}}, accessed 5 June 2010"}}
